A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PreMIO research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite restructuring.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original solver experiments on multi-knapsack, set covering, and IEEE 118 security-constrained unit commitment instances.

after.justification: Section 4 retains those experiments and adds branching-rule and data-free MIPLIB results. Appendix D also provides an empirical parameter-selection illustration.

M1.justification: The basic cardinality branching algorithm remains, but v2 adds objective-cut pruning of the other three branches in Section 3.2 and a procedure for selecting τ and δ using training data in Appendix D. It removes v1's multiple-threshold and redundant-constraint identification extensions. The LP-relaxation surrogate already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on general MIPLIB instances without offline training data, starting from 132 instances and reporting aggregate results for 57 retained instances. MKP, SCP, and IEEE 118 SCUC coverage remains. It also evaluates complete branching solves on MKP beyond the earlier primal-solution experiments.

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same Gurobi and COPT solvers and their heuristic configurations, comparing performance with and without PreMIO. The new experiments also use these existing solver comparators; no additional learned baseline is evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 replaces arithmetic mean runtimes with shifted geometric means using a shift of 10 and reverses the written speedup ratio to Original/PreMIO. New branching experiments specify four Gurobi threads, 3600 seconds, and 0.015%/0.01% gaps. The MIPLIB protocol adds a 3600-second limit and excludes immediately infeasible preferred branches and paired timeouts.

E4.justification: The existing study of solver heuristic levels remains. V2 adds targeted parameter analyses: Table 2 compares three δ/τ configurations on MIPLIB, while Appendix D and Figure 2 examine SCUC prediction accuracy versus τ and illustrate selecting δ.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed experiments, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The revised runtime aggregation changes the evaluation metric; the theoretical probability bounds do not constitute empirical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: V2 replaces SCP and SCUC summaries under the revised aggregation; for example, Gurobi's SCP (1000,10000,L) value changes from 12.932 to 9.08. MKP values remain equivalent up to rounding. New results include branching-runtime SGMs of 28.7 versus 25.8 and 1283 versus 979, and a MIPLIB relative SGM of 0.84. Cross-version changes under different aggregation do not establish performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The central assumptions, VC bound, Theorems 1–3, and their retained proofs remain essentially unchanged. V1's redundant-constraint Lemma 2 and Appendix C.2 proof are removed. V2 adds pruning reasoning and Appendix D's accuracy definitions and δ derivation, and corrects the sample indexing in Definition 2.

C1.justification: The central claims of simple, explainable, solver-compatible acceleration through learned cardinality branching remain. V2 drops v1's explicit data-privacy contribution claim and its abstract's quantified claim that integration requires two lines of code.

C2.justification: V2 adds specific applicability limits for the previously outlined data-free extension: weak LP relaxations can produce infeasible preferred regions, and competitive performance requires very conservative δ values. It also interprets complete-solve benefits as smaller than primal-heuristic benefits. The original risk-pooling explanation remains.

D1.justification: V2 specifies interior-point LP predictions, settings for the new experiments, and practical tuning instructions. It omits v1's explicit CPLEX 12.1.0 version and the SCUC rule for fixing predictions constant across training instances. These omissions establish reduced documentation, not that the underlying settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to Fischetti and Lodi's Local Branching, the ML4CO competition report, and MIPLIB 2017. The existing literature coverage and positioning around solver-compatible learning and cardinality branching otherwise remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites the abstract and extensively edits explanatory prose throughout Sections 1–3. It restructures the practical extensions and separates experiments into setup, primal heuristic, branching rule, and data-free evaluation sections. Appendix D changes from numerical statistics to hyperparameter tuning.

P2.justification: V2 removes the conceptual branching illustration and redraws v1's three benchmark plots as one three-panel figure with numerical labels and a logarithmic MKP axis that displays previously clipped values. The old appendix statistics table disappears, while three new experimental tables and a two-panel tuning figure are introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 adds evidence for previously untested uses, clarifies the speedup metric, and improves numerical displays. However, its new guidance contains material inconsistencies: Section 3.2 claims pruning when the preferred branch excludes all optima, while Appendix D maximizes error indicators labeled accuracy and selects τ ≈ 0.1 despite specifying τ ≥ 0.5. These problems undermine the reliability of important additions, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
